nm_south_organs.blurb: South Organs lies at the southern end of the Organ Mountains near Las Cruces, New Mexico, south of Fillmore Canyon. Nearly everything here is bouldering, and almost all of it sits at Pena Blanca, a sprawling spread of boulder problems at the southern foot of the range. A handful of short sport and trad routes and a few top-ropes round it out. Boulder grades run from V0 to V7, with the bulk in the easier V0 to V3 range and a thinner tail of harder problems. Roped climbs run from low 5th class to 5.11. Long Canyon and Achenbach Canyon hold far fewer climbs.

qc_l_amphitheatre.blurb: L'Amphitheatre is a quartzite crag at Saint-Andre-de-Kamouraska, in Quebec's Bas-Saint-Laurent region. Sport climbing dominates, with a good number of top-rope lines and only a few trad routes. The walls are divided into thirteen sub-areas, among them La tache noire, Bonsai and Hommage à Radoth, each holding a modest number of lines. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.12, weighted toward 5.10 to 5.12, with a fair spread of easier routes between 5.5 and 5.9 as well. The routes are described as covering all levels, which makes it workable for mixed groups.

ri_pond_cave_area.blurb: Pond Cave Area is a bouldering zone inside Lincoln Woods State Park, a short distance from Providence, Rhode Island. The boulders of Lincoln Woods are coarse granite, and the climbing here is entirely bouldering. Problems run from V0 into double-digit grades, with the bulk between V0 and V4. Pond Cave itself is a longer cliff band almost over a pond and holds some of the steepest climbing in the woods. It is described as getting winter sun and summer shade, though summer brings mosquitoes and the approach can be muddy. Other sub-areas include Northeast Area, The Talus Area and Fatboy Boulder.

az_aspen_trail_boulders.blurb: Aspen Trail Boulders is a bouldering area up on Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains of southern Arizona. All of the climbing is boulder problems, spread across thirteen sub-areas. Gandalf's Gorge holds the most climbs, followed by River Boulder and Ronald's Chasm. Grades run from very easy up to V12, with a broad middle from V1 to V6 and a good number of harder problems above. Gandalf's Gorge is a canyon with a streambed, and its rock is described as crumbly and sharp, with a few boulders singled out as the better ones. The area is described as good for summer bouldering, with a stream, trees and shade for a day's circuit.
